item.title: E-R Model of Redis Cluster
item.description:
The Redis module organizes production Redis into clusters. A cluster is a logical entity with Redis instances on one or more nodes.

Each cluster is an autonomous, high-performance cache or storage unit with at least one Redis instance. It exposes services through ports.

There are three core entities in Pigsty’s Redis module:

  • Cluster: An autonomous Redis service unit and the top-level namespace for other entities.
  • Instance: One Redis server process using a specific port on a node.
  • Node: An implicitly declared hardware resource that runs Linux and Systemd. It can host multiple Redis instances.

Redis usually runs multiple instances per node, unlike PostgreSQL. This uses multiple CPU cores on a physical server or VM. Nodes and instances therefore have a 1:N relationship. For production, Redis instances with more than 12 GB of memory are generally discouraged.

item.title: Module: REDIS
item.description:
REDIS is Pigsty’s Redis-compatible cache module. Select Redis or Valkey with redis_type. The default remains redis. Both engines support primary-replica replication, Sentinel, and native cluster mode. They share configuration paths, instance service names, monitoring, and log entry points.

redis_type: redis  # default; valkey is also supported

The role installs the selected engine and redis-exporter. Instance processes use redis-server / redis-cli or valkey-server / valkey-cli, respectively. A change to redis_type changes packages and binaries. It does not automatically validate data formats, replication topology, or rollback. Rehearse any engine change on an existing cluster. Use the same engine throughout a logical cluster.

item.title: Configuration
item.description:
Concept

The Redis entity model is similar to the PostgreSQL model. It includes Cluster and Instance entities. Here, Cluster does not mean native Redis Cluster mode.

REDIS uses a single-node multi-instance deployment. PGSQL uses a 1:1 deployment. Multiple Redis instances typically share one physical or virtual node to use multiple CPU cores. Thus, the procedures to configure and administer Redis instances differ slightly from PGSQL.

In Pigsty, each Redis node belongs to one cluster. You cannot deploy instances from two different Redis clusters on the same node.

item.title: Playbook
item.description:
The REDIS module provides two playbooks for deploying/removing Redis clusters/nodes/instances:

  • redis.yml: Deploy Redis cluster/node/instance
  • redis-rm.yml: Remove Redis cluster/node/instance

redis.yml

The redis.yml playbook for deploying Redis contains the following subtasks:

redis_node : Init redis node
 - redis_install : Install Redis and the `redis-exporter` package
 - redis_user : Create OS user redis
 - redis_dir : Configure redis FHS directory structure
redis_exporter : Configure redis_exporter monitoring
 - redis_exporter_config : Generate redis_exporter config
 - redis_exporter_launch : Launch redis_exporter
redis_instance : Init and restart redis cluster/node/instance
 - redis_config : Generate redis instance config
 - redis_launch : Launch redis instance
redis_register : Register redis to infrastructure
redis_ha : Configure redis sentinel (sentinel mode only)
redis_join : Join redis native cluster (cluster mode only)

item.title: Metrics
item.description:
This page separates raw metrics from scrape endpoints from recorded metrics computed by vmalert. files/victoria/rules/redis.yml defines 96 recording rules. Common examples appear below; the Recording Metric Index lists every name and expression. Query recorded metrics in VictoriaMetrics, not at an exporter’s /metrics endpoint.

Raw metrics vary with software versions, collectors, privileges, instance roles, and runtime state. Historical scrape samples are retained for identifying metrics, not as a complete interface for the current version.

item.title: FAQ
item.description:
ABORT due to redis_safeguard enabled

This means the Redis instance you are trying to remove has the safeguard enabled. If redis_safeguard is true, redis-rm.yml always refuses to run. The switch does not check whether an instance is running.

First, confirm the exact -l/redis_port target, a recent backup, and the redis_rm_data setting. Then use -e redis_safeguard=false to override the protection and run removal. This switch only disables the guard. It does not verify the target or recovery capability.
